record.title: FAM-010 chemotherapy for canine splenic hemangiosarcoma — enrolling soon
record.center: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital
record.status: Enrolling soon; study inquiries accepted through the sponsor form. Confirm the next dose-group opening with the study team.
record.status_confidence_basis: Current published protocol and observed functioning inquiry form; owner explicitly approved this upcoming listing. This does not confirm that treatment enrollment is open.
record.contacts: Use Contact the study team on the official Familiar study page. The form connects eligible inquiries with the Illinois team; confirm when a dose group can start.
record.funding: Familiar covers study screening, FAM-010 treatment and study follow-up care. Owners pay travel to and from Urbana. Coverage of the preceding splenectomy or unrelated care is not specified.
record.intervention: Investigational albumin-linked doxorubicin (FAM-010), given by intravenous infusion every three weeks. Six treatments are planned initially; some dogs may receive up to twelve. All study dogs receive FAM-010; no placebo.
record.special_requirement: Enrollment is announced as enrolling soon; ask about the next dose group before arranging care. Splenic hemangiosarcoma must be confirmed by pathology before joining, but owners awaiting results or with splenectomy scheduled may inquire now. The first dose must be possible within 21 days after splenectomy. No previous chemotherapy, radiation or other investigational drug; no intended breeding. Regular Urbana visits are required. This initial study establishes dose and side effects; improved survival and reduced heart toxicity are not established. Permanent infertility is expected in intact male dogs.
record.notes: FAM-010 links doxorubicin to albumin to investigate whether drug delivery and heart safety can be improved. This first canine study focuses on dose and tolerability; it does not establish better survival or cardiac safety. Eligible dogs have splenic hemangiosarcoma and recent or planned splenectomy. Pathology can be pending at inquiry but must confirm the diagnosis before enrollment. The first dose must fit within 21 days after surgery; entry may be delayed between small dose groups. Previous chemotherapy, radiation or another investigational drug excludes entry. Dogs intended for breeding are excluded; permanent infertility is expected in intact males. The sponsor covers study screening, drug treatment and study follow-up; travel is owner-paid, and prior surgery coverage is not stated.
